summary: The audit fixes are real. The ring_low leg inserts now sit on the 22 mm lug's centre line with 9 mm of wall to each edge. A new landing FEA covers the lugs, and legs, hub and roll ring now print flat on the bed. Teardrops, grommets plus inserts, SF 3 and the voltage-derated T/W are all in place, and the gimbal, props and electrics check out. One major problem remains: the 'mass' requirement passes at 745.4 g against 750 g only because the three carbon tubes (catalog density 1.5, about 12.9 g together), the XT60 and every fastener, insert and dowel are counted as 0 g. The real all-up mass is about 765-770 g, which fails the declared limit, although T/W at 22.2 V stays at about 2.1.

findings.issue: report.json purchased mass_g is 0.0 for rod_1, rod_2, rod_3 and xt60. kerf/checks.py item_mass_g only reads weight_g/mass_g, and rods.cf_tube_5x3 has only od/id/density: 3 x pi/4 x (5^2 - 3^2) x 228 mm x 1.5 g/cm3 = 12.9 g. The XT60 has no weight. Fasteners (about 30 screws, 13 heat-set inserts, 2 dowels, 9 set screws) are not counted either. 745.4 g (683.3 parts + 62.1 wiring) is really about 765-770 g, over the 750 g mass_max that the twr 'why' says it is sized at. twr then falls to about 2.11 and twr_sag to about 1.89, both still above their limits. leg_fea and lug_fea use 729 g.
findings.fix: Engine (would hit every rod project): in item_mass_g, compute rod mass from catalog density x annulus area x the item's length, and add a test. Add a sourced weight_g to drone.connectors.XT60. Optionally add fastener mass from the fastener report. Then either trim mass or raise mass_max with the twr margin as the reason, and re-run cg/tip_over/twr/flight_time and the leg/lug load cases at the real mass.

findings.issue: DESIGN.md, STATUS.md and the ring_low docstring say the bosses, webs and lug ribs touch the bed. They do not. In print orientation only the four 4 mm yoke-bridge webs (18 tall) reach z 0: STL bed contact is 1464 mm². The tube-boss ends float 4 mm up (14 tall) and the lug ribs 8 mm up (10 tall), and the 7222 mm² plate face is 18 mm up on supports. A 124 g, 111 mm tall part standing on four thin strips is acceptable on textured PEI with supports, but marginal, and the documentation is wrong.
findings.fix: Make the bed-contact features one height. Trim the bridge webs to 14 mm (flush with the bosses, then re-run yoke_fea) or raise the bosses to 18 mm (longer tube engagement). Do not raise the 30-degree rib to 18 mm: the ph_top/servo route point [26.8, 20, 100] passes about 4 mm from that rib's centre line at z 100. Correct the text.

findings.issue: A-5 is only partly done. The radial M3 lock taps in ring_mid and ring_top are plain cylinders, horizontal in print with no teardrop (ring_low's have teardrops). The leg's two M3 clearance holes are horizontal in the on-its-side print (bolt_pattern without teardrop).
findings.fix: Use iface.hole(..., teardrop=iface.print_up_deg(ctx, loc)) for the ring_mid/ring_top lock taps, and pass teardrop= to the leg bolt_pattern.

findings.issue: A-11 is only partly done. The leg root fillet is there. The hub fork/arm-to-disc roots, gimbal_outer pad-to-ring corners and ring_low gusset/lug roots have no fillets, and no part has outside-edge chamfers (ENGINEERING.md s5).
findings.fix: Add 1.5-2 mm fillets at the hub arm and fork roots and the lug and bridge roots, plus 0.6 mm bed-edge chamfers (elephant foot).

findings.issue: lug_fea passes on p99.9 8.08 vs 13 MPa, but its volume peak is 21.70 MPa (1.7x the limit; surface peak 11.23) on a coarse 4935-element mesh of a 194 mm part. The peak location is not reported. In the render the hot zone is the disc and lug roots near the wire pass, which is the expected load path.
findings.fix: Refine the mesh (or have the engine report peak_at like max_disp_at) and confirm the 21.7 MPa peak is a load-patch singularity, not the lug-to-disc root. Fillet that root (see above).

findings.issue: The 5x3 pultruded CF tubes (1 mm wall) are held only by 9 cup-point set screws on filed flats. A point load on a 1 mm pultruded wall cracks it lengthwise, and 'stop at first contact + 1/8 turn' leaves the mast relying on that friction in a crash.
findings.fix: Bond the tubes with epoxy in the bores (keep the set screws only for alignment while it cures), or use nylon-tip set screws as the default rather than the alternative.

findings.issue: Stale numbers remain. The XT60 row says 'hover 11.8 A, peak 36.6 A' (report: 12.2 / 43.8 A). The mass row says 745 g, which leaves out the uncounted tubes and fasteners (see the major finding).
findings.fix: Refresh from report.json after the mass fix.
